title: Dental PPO vs. dental HMO insurance plans
summary: Compares dental PPO and dental HMO insurance plans, including a side-by-side table and pros and cons of each.

atoms.title: Dental HMO and dental PPO plans
atoms.question: What are the two most common types of dental insurance?
atoms.text: Dental health maintenance organization (DHMO) and dental preferred provider organization (DPPO) plans are the two most common dental insurance plans. UnitedHealthcare says one option is not better than the other; each type has its own advantages and limitations.
questions: What are the types of dental insurance?
Is dental PPO or HMO better?

atoms.title: Dental PPO versus dental HMO at a glance
atoms.question: What is the difference between PPO and HMO dental insurance?
atoms.text: A dental PPO is best for more control and flexibility, with higher premiums, a broad network, partial out-of-network reimbursement that likely costs less with a network provider, no primary care dentist or specialist referral required, an annual maximum, and sometimes a copay. A dental HMO is best for affordability, with lower premiums, a smaller network, no out-of-network coverage, a required primary care dentist and referrals, no annual maximum, and copays.

Which dental plan has an annual maximum?
Do dental HMO plans require referrals?

atoms.title: What a dental PPO plan is
atoms.question: What is dental PPO insurance?
atoms.text: A dental preferred provider organization (DPPO) plan is a type of insurance that offers members broad access to pre-selected providers. These dentists and specialists have already agreed to participate in the insurance company's network, which usually makes it cheaper and easier to see providers within that network.
questions: What does PPO mean for dental insurance?
How does a dental PPO work?

atoms.title: Advantages of dental PPO plans
atoms.question: What are the pros of a dental PPO plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists four pros of dental PPO plans: greater flexibility in choosing a dentist, since members can visit network or out-of-network providers; lower costs for services, with deeper discounts for in-network care; no referral required to see a specialist; and possible partial reimbursement for out-of-network services, depending on the plan.
questions: Can I see any dentist with a PPO?
Do I need a referral to see a dental specialist on a PPO?

atoms.title: Drawbacks of dental PPO plans
atoms.question: What are the cons of a dental PPO plan?
atoms.text: Cons of dental PPO plans include higher monthly premiums than HMO plans, in exchange for flexibility and more options. A PPO plan requires meeting a deductible, a set amount paid for dental care before benefits start to pay, which resets every 12 months. Coinsurance, a percentage of the cost of a procedure, also tends to be higher with PPO dental plans than with HMO plans.
questions: Do dental PPO plans have a deductible?
Are dental PPO premiums higher than HMO?

atoms.title: When a dental PPO may be right for you
atoms.question: Is PPO dental insurance right for me?
atoms.text: A dental PPO plan is a good choice for someone who wants more flexibility in choosing a provider and the ability to see a specialist without a referral. UnitedHealthcare adds that if a person knows they will need more care in the coming year and can budget for higher premiums, a PPO dental plan might be right for them.

atoms.title: What a dental HMO plan is
atoms.question: What is dental HMO insurance?
atoms.text: A dental health maintenance organization (DHMO) is a budget-oriented plan designed to help lower the cost of care. These plans emphasize preventive care and prioritize regular check-ups with a primary dental facility or provider.
questions: What does HMO mean for dental insurance?
How does a dental HMO work?

atoms.title: Advantages of dental HMO plans
atoms.question: What are the pros of a dental HMO plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists three pros of dental HMO plans. Lower monthly premiums and out-of-pocket costs, since they work with a network of providers at reduced rates. Usually no deductible or annual maximum, because the plans focus on preventive care and routine procedures. Fixed copays, a predetermined flat rate listed in the benefits for covered services, which makes dental costs easier to budget.
questions: Do dental HMO plans have deductibles?
Are dental HMO plans cheaper?
How do copays work on a dental HMO?

atoms.title: Drawbacks of dental HMO plans
atoms.question: What are the cons of a dental HMO plan?
atoms.text: Cons of dental HMO plans include a restricted network, since a member selects a primary care dentist from a smaller network of covered providers. Care outside the HMO's network is not covered. Seeing a specialist requires a referral from the primary care dentist, and without a referral, dental services may not be covered by the plan.
questions: Does a dental HMO cover out-of-network dentists?
Do I need a referral for a dental specialist on an HMO?

atoms.title: When a dental HMO may be right for you
atoms.question: Is HMO dental insurance right for me?
atoms.text: If flexibility and frequent specialist care are not a top priority, a dental HMO plan could be the best bet, and UnitedHealthcare calls DHMO plans a great option when affordability and low dental costs are the main concerns. The plans work best for people who want to stick with a primary dentist to coordinate care and are comfortable obtaining referrals for specialist care.
